I'm using a Dell Pro 14 Plus, asset ID LA339701.

The Windows Updates that came in over the weekend were:

2026-05 .NET Framework Security Update (KB5087051)
2026-05 Security Update (Hotpatch capable) (KB5089466) (26200.8390)

I'm running Windows 11 25H2 (platypus) and I'm a member of the ETD early adopters group for desktop updates, if that's what may have caused it.

Hope this helps! Cheers.

Joshua

short_description: Follow-up: Release timing – Data Management Function (AFDA V2) – NAA1000439699
description:
Hello Frankie,  NAA Information Management Team,

I am writing to follow up on the status of the Data Management function within AFDA V2 (inquiry reference: NAA1000439699).

As noted in previous correspondence, DEWR provided feedback on the draft in August 2025 and understands that the National Archives of Australia (NAA) has been incorporating agency input and progressing revisions. The previous update indicated that release was anticipated around April 2026, we are seeking advice on the current status and expected next steps.
DEWR context and dependency

  *   DEWR is currently on hold with the development of our internal Data Retention and Disposal Policy and Procedures
  *   This is pending the outcome and release of the NAA government-wide Data Management function
  *   Timely release is critical to ensure alignment with whole-of-government disposal authorities and avoid rework or compliance risks

Request
We would appreciate your advice on:

  *   Status of the AFDA V2 Data Management function
  *   Expected timeframe for final release
  *   Any opportunities for further agency input, if applicable

We acknowledge the significance of this work and appreciate your continued efforts to progress this through to release, as it will support the current work of DEWR and other agencies.

Please let me know if a short discussion would assist.


regards
Phill

What are the delegate permission levels in Outlook?
You can set delegate permissions in the following ways:

  *   Reviewer: With this permission, the delegate can read items in your folders.
  *   Author: With this permission, the delegate can read and create items, and change and delete items that they create. For example, a delegate can create meeting requests directly in your Mail or Calendar folder and then send the item on your behalf.
  *   Editor: With this permission, the delegate can do everything that an Author has permission to do and additionally can change and delete the items that you created.
If the delegate tries to perform an action that they don't have permissions for, they'll get an error message to let them know they can't perform that task.

Subject: Safe Work Australia- Meeting to Discuss Moving from Service Request to RITA and SSO Configuration Requirements

Hello,

At the end of 2026, our existing Mobility Service Request (SR) platform will reach end of life and be decommissioned. In preparation, RITA has been developed and released, and all clients currently using the SR platform will need to migrate to RITA. Our initial focus has been on migrating our WOAG clients.

RITA is a newly developed solution by Cushman & Wakefield, designed to streamline the logging of Facilities Management service requests. It retains all existing SR functionality while introducing an enhanced user interface, a comprehensive work order detail page, and additional features that we will continue to expand over time. During the transition period, both SR and RITA will operate concurrently until SR is fully decommissioned.

RITA supports Single Sign-On (SSO) configuration. For clients, such as yourself, who currently access SR using a username and password, we would like to engage with you to discuss the available SSO options and do some testing.
Attached are the SSO configuration documents for both RITA and the Service Request application, along with a copy of the RITA user guide, for your reference.

If you would like to learn more, please let me know your availability next week. I’d be happy to schedule a 20?minute meeting to walk through the solution and test your access to RITA.
If you would prefer me to engage with someone else within your entity, please send me their details and I can reach out.

short_description: Clarification on Process for Returning Records to the Department
description:
Good morning

We are seeking clarification on the current process for returning records to the Department.

Earlier this year, we received guidance (outlined below) and would like to confirm whether this remains the recommended approach.

By way of background, we are currently transitioning to new Deeds for our providers. The existing Deeds are due to expire at the end of July, and providers are required to return all documentation held-both physical and digital. This spans six providers and covers records dating back up to seven years. It has been confirmed that these records are not to be destroyed. As you can appreciate, the volume of documentation is expected to be significant.

The previous advice indicated that providers should complete a records register prior to returning documentation. Given the scale of records involved, we are seeking confirmation on whether this remains best practice, or if an alternative approach would be acceptable.

We would appreciate any updated guidance or recommendations to support an efficient and compliant return process. We note there is reference to a supplementary Records Management Instructions guide and would be grateful if you could provide a copy for distribution to our providers.

Rebecca

Subject: FW: Procedure for return of paper records from Registered Training Organisations (RTO) [SEC=OFFICIAL]

Hi team,

Apologies for the delay in response to your query from mid-December, we have only just today received the below advice from the Information Management and SharePoint team.

Hopefully, this information is helpful. If you have further questions, the IM&S team are happy to assist. You can contact them by email informationmanagementinbox@dewr.gov.au<mailto:informationmanagementinbox@dewr.gov.au> or submit a ticket in the service desk portal.

Service Desk Portal<https://dese.service-now.com/servicedeskportal>

Hi Emma,

Thanks for your patience.  Information Management and SharePoint (IM&S) Team can facilitate a transfer process for RTO providers to send back both physical and digital records.  This will be an adapted version of the one use for Workforce Australia and Apprenticeship providers.

Depending on the retention requirements for the records the providers may also be able to destroy records that have met their retention requirements and report this destruction to the department.

To process returns we will need a completed records register which lists what the provider plans to return.  I have attached an example.

Once we have reviewed the register and confirmed it is complete we will

for digital returns - provide instructions to complete a digital transfer to the department using a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP).  The records must be provided in a flat structure with a single file per participant which only contains documents (no nested sub-folders).  Only the top folder should be zipped.  Do not zip the lower folders as this is unnecessary and will make processing more complex.  Once the records are uploaded and then downloaded and imported by IM&S the provider can destroy the version they have in line with the contract.

for physical returns - organise boxes and barcodes to be delivered directly to the provider's nominated address for the records to be packaged up for transfer.  Once affixed to the boxes the barcodes must be added to the register so that the records can be identified within each box.  Once the completed register including barcodes is received and verified by IM&S, transport can be organised (the provider pays for the transport) and we will import the records into our system.

Digital information management is an expectation across the department and with service providers.  If this is not yet a requirement it should be included in the next contract review for this business function.  This can be supported by a set of supplementary Records Management Instructions to guide the providers through the return process.  This is how the other programs manage this process.

I can provide further instruction on how to complete the spreadsheet and organise the digital records for transfer if required.  Happy to discuss if you have any questions.

Thanks, and have a great day
Julie Carpenter

short_description: For advice – ACER inquiry on LANTITE candidate data retention and Commonwealth records
description:
OFFICIAL: Sensitive

Good afternoon Information Management Team

We are seeking your advice on a few data?retention and record?management questions raised by our contracted supplier, the Australian Council for Educational Research (ACER), in relation to the Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education Students (LANTITE) program<https://www.education.gov.au/teaching-and-school-leadership/literacy-and-numeracy-test-initial-teacher-education>. We have sought input from Education’s Office of the Chief Data Officer (OCDO) (email attachment 1), and the Privacy Team (email attachment 2). Both areas have suggested that we confirm a few matters with your team.

Background
ACER has received a request from a former LANTITE candidate (LANTITE standards met in May 2019; results issued June 2019) seeking deletion of their ACER candidate account. ACER has written to confirm with the department that, under the LANTITE contract (email attachment 3), they are required to retain Commonwealth records for seven years after the relevant record is finalised (i.e. until June 2026 in this case). We have also provided the Privacy Impact Assessment if helpful (email attachment 4).

Arising from this inquiry, ACER’s legal team has raised a few follow?up questions and is seeking clarification from the department:

  1.  How long ACER may retain personal information collected as part of LANTITE, having regard to contractual obligations, the Privacy Act, and Commonwealth recordkeeping requirements.
  2.  Which elements of the personal information ACER collects constitute Commonwealth records, and whether this applies to all or only some categories of candidate data.
  3.  Whether, at the end of a contract cycle, all Commonwealth records may (or should) be transferred to the Department, rather than retained by ACER.

In this context, ACER’s psychometricians have advised that removing a candidate's personal data will not diminish ACER's ability to perform its required psychometric and statistical work. ACER retains a remnant record of the candidate in data files, which removes all information that could be used to personally identify the candidate, but which retains the following:

  *   Metadata about the specific test form sat
  *   Information about the test window(s) the candidate sat in
  *   Responses to individual items
  *   Raw and scale scores achieved
  *   Standard achieved/not achieved status

ACER has also advised that a ‘dummy’ ID could be assigned in place of this candidate’s ID such that it will be possible for them to identify that this candidate’s PI has been removed as per their request, if we ever need such information.

For advice:
Building on advice received from the Privacy team and the OCDO while noting the department’s obligations under the Archives Act 1983 (Archives Act) and Privacy Act 1988 (Privacy Act), we would appreciate your advice on the following:

  1.  Whether there would be any permitted reason for the destruction of Commonwealth records (i.e. personal information collected by ACER as part of LANTITE) in the outlined circumstances (for example, where ACER retains a remnant record (e.g. with a ‘dummy ID’) and the original candidate account may be considered a duplicate, and therefore could be deleted).
  2.  The applicable retention period for these Commonwealth records under the Archives Act (including minimum retention periods for these records).
  3.  The most appropriate way for the department to manage Commonwealth records held by ACER following finalisation of the Contract.
  4.  Whether any categories of Commonwealth records could be lawfully destroyed by the department or ACER.

We are comfortable to proceed on the basis of a standard turnaround timeframe of 10 business days, if appropriate for your team.

Many thanks

We have previously sought advice from the Information Management team in DEWR about records management practices and retention policies - advice attached.

The "Contact Us<https://www.studyassist.gov.au/contact-us>" form on the StudyAssist website uses Qualtrics.  This Qualtrics form is about to be updated as part of the CRM Project and will now require students to attach their ID e.g. driver's license, passport etc. to the form when they contact the Department.  They will only need to do this for queries related to the www.myhelpbalance.gov.au<http://www.myhelpbalance.gov.au> (mHb) website. Currently for mHb related enquiries, current procedure involves staff sending a reply email asking students to email in their ID. This new form will simplify the process, requesting photo ID upfront, therefore reducing the number of emails between students and the department.

For the new process, when a student uses the "Contact Us" form on the mHb website and uploads their ID as an attachment, a record will be created in the CRM which lists the details of the query and has a URL that links to the Qualtrics ID attachment location. The ID is never stored in the CRM or Outlook and always remains inside Qualtrics via the URL. Access to this URL is based on a departmental user having a Qualtrics account.

Question
Are these Qualtrics ID records (ie; URL) subject to retention rules advised in the attachment?  If so, how long must they be kept and where must they be stored i.e. Qualtrics, SharePoint etc?

Importantly to note, a photo ID is considered sensitive information, whereas the enquiry itself is just considered personal information.

short_description: Seeking advice: changes in data retention policy social media
description:
Hi team,

We've been informed that the data retention policy for our social media management platform is changing from seven years to one. I'm exploring other avenues for archiving required information to ensure we're meeting our obligations.

I'm seeking clarity on what exactly should be archived in a social media context. All approvals are already saved in a separate system as are any images or videos we post. The type of information that is current captured/archived by our social media management platform is as follows:

  *   Comments from the public on the department's social media content
  *   Comments related to the department that are posted on other people's content (social listening)
  *   Results on social media posts like how far they've reached and how many people interacted with the content (likes, web clicks etc)

We use the above for internal reporting and performance tracking, so it is captured in part through those mechanisms, but I'd like to confirm if that's enough or whether the detail of each post needs to be kept.

Diane

Hi Service Desk,

May we please seek assistance from the relevant team (presumably one of Platform or Gateway Services teams) with actioning the below request from the Department of Finance?

Context
Finance administers the Organisations and Appointments Register (OAR), which serves as a backend to the Government Online Directory<https://www.directory.gov.au/> as well as the source for various transparency reporting products on Government appointments. OAR is delivered on the Salesforce platform and requires data maintenance by each department for their respective portfolio. A number of key functions, such as the creation or cessation of government entities, must be progressed as a task within OAR that ultimately requires administrator action by Finance.

Based on Finance's request below (and supplementary advice attached), we understand that a recent policy change by Salesforce<https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_general_verify_email_domain.htm&release=260&type=5&utm_source=techcomms&utm_campaign=FY27_Core_4168847> means these key tasks will now no longer notify Finance when provisioned by users within the DEWR domain, leaking to a reasonable risk of oversight. This potentially impacts the functions of Parliamentary's appointments reporting team, WR Group's appointments team, and the SES Unit (all copied for info). The Department of Education is also required to update this system - so you may receive a similar request from their appointments team, if you have not already.

Finance have now reached out seeking for DEWR's email domain to be validated in Salesforce to rectify this issue, per steps listed below. Grateful if you could please notify MinisterialAppointments@dewr.gov.au<mailto:MinisterialAppointments@dewr.gov.au> once actioned, as Finance will need this confirmation to complete actions on their end.

If more information on the request is necessary, I'd suggest reaching out to Ruwan.Lokusooriya@finance.gov.au<mailto:Ruwan.Lokusooriya@finance.gov.au> and OAR@finance.gov.au<mailto:OAR@finance.gov.au> at Finance, who would be best-placed to assist with technical detail.

short_description: Query re record keeping of ID verification documents
description:
Good afternoon

I am a Senior Policy Officer within the VET Student Loans (VSL) Policy and Students Team. I am reaching out to your team to get an understanding of the legislated record keeping requirements of identification documents.

Currently, when VSL students, or former VET FEE-HELP (VFH) students contact our team, or apply for re-credits of debt, we request documentation from them to verify their identity to ensure we are speaking to and sharing information with the person themselves. At the moment, when the ID documents are provided to us by the individual, they are not destroyed and are kept as part of their email file records.

My question is, under the Archives Act 1983, is the department authorised or required to de-identify or destroy identity documents which are received for the purposes of verifying the identity of the person who makes a request to access their personal information held by the department?

Any other advice you can provide about this process would also be appreciated.

Kind regards
Courtney
